question: An article is sold for ₹240 with a loss of 20%. What is the cost price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fractional value of 20% = 1/5

Let Cost Price = 5 units, Loss = 1 unit

Selling Price = 5 − 1 = 4 units

Given 4 units = ₹240 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹60

Cost Price = 5 units = 5 × 60 = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹240

Loss Percentage = 20%

 
 Cost Price
 ? (100%)
 
 
 Selling Price
 ₹240 (80%)
 
 
• 
 

 −20% Loss

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (240 × 100) ÷ (100 − 20)

⇒ CP = (240 × 100) ÷ 80

⇒ CP = 3 × 100

⇒ CP = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). The formula relates them as: SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.
